title: Variational Quantum Classifiers
summary: Classify points in the plane with two qubits and data re-uploading.
objectives: Load data into a circuit as rotation angles and load it again between trainable layers
Train a classifier and judge it on points it has not seen
Recognize overfitting from the gap between training and test accuracy
mission: No straight line separates the two concentric circles, so the classifier needs a curved boundary. Train a quantum classifier whose sign of ⟨Z⟩ on qubit 0 is the predicted class, with at least 92% accuracy on a test set that you do not see.

prediction.question: The data enter the circuit only once (LAYERS = 1), and everything else is trained as well as possible. What accuracy can you expect on the two circles?
options: Above 95%: the trainable rotations make up for loading the data once
It does not exceed 50%: with so little freedom the output is no better than chance
Around 70%: above chance, but the output is too low in frequency to fit circles
prediction.explanation: With a single upload the output is a trigonometric function of degree 1 in each coordinate, so the boundary is stiff, but it still carries some information about the radius and beats chance. Training gives about 70% on this data. Re-uploading the data in several layers raises the frequencies the circuit can represent, and with 3 layers the test accuracy is above 95%.

hints: The starter circuit uses LAYERS = 1. What would change if the data entered several times instead of once?
Raise LAYERS to 3: each layer applies trainable rotations and loads x again. Then train with qml.AdamOptimizer(0.1), updating weights = optimizer.step(loss, weights) for about 40 epochs.
Append float(loss(weights)) to history at every epoch. If training accuracy is high but test accuracy is low, the model has memorized the points: train for fewer epochs or use fewer layers.

messages.ok: Accuracy of {test}% on the test set (threshold {threshold}%), and {train}% on the training set.
messages.no_circuit: The QNode circuit(weights, x) is missing: define it so that it returns qml.expval(qml.PauliZ(0)).
messages.no_weights: The trained weights are missing: store them in the variable weights.
messages.overfit: Accuracy {train}% on the training set but only {test}% on the test set: the model has memorized the training points. Use fewer layers or fewer epochs.
messages.no_reupload: Accuracy {test}% on the test set (threshold {threshold}%). The data enter the circuit only {uploads} times, too few to curve the boundary: load x again in several layers.
messages.low_accuracy: Accuracy {test}% on the test set (threshold {threshold}%). The circuit loads the data enough times, so the training is the problem: more epochs or a different learning rate.

challenge.mission: The mission used two qubits, and it is fair to ask whether the second one did any of the work. The frequencies in the output come from the number of uploads, so one qubit should be enough. Build a classifier on a single qubit for the same circles: define circuit(weights, x), which takes x of shape (N, 2) as in the mission and returns qml.expval(qml.PauliZ(0)), train it on X_train and keep the result in weights. The validator traces the circuit and requires every gate to act on one and the same qubit, then measures the accuracy of the sign of ⟨Z⟩ on 300 new points of the same two circles, which no training touched, and requires at least 90%.
hints: With one qubit there is no CNOT and no partner to correlate with. What does the prediction of this lesson say about the number of times x enters?

Replace the two wires by one: in each layer apply qml.Rot(*weights[layer], wires=0), then qml.RX(x[:, 0], wires=0) and qml.RY(x[:, 1], wires=0). End with one more Rot before the measurement. weights then has shape (LAYERS + 1, 3).

Start with LAYERS = 4 and train with qml.AdamOptimizer(0.1) for about 60 epochs. If the test accuracy stays low while the training accuracy is high, you have memorized the 80 points: use fewer layers. If both are low, load x more times or train longer.
